actionable_steps.step: Reduce your desires day by day — lighten the luggage of desires that overshadows your happiness.

actionable_steps.step: Give up evil qualities, evil practices, ego, and unsacred feelings — that is true renunciation.

actionable_steps.step: Carry on your duties with faith in God — detachment will develop of its own accord as love of God grows.

actionable_steps.step: Discharge the duties of your own stage of life and sanctify your time by contemplating on God.

actionable_steps.citation: Alms and Qualms — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 9 (1969), 1969-01-13
actionable_steps.step: Be content — God will grant you what you need and deserve; there is no need to ask, no reason to grumble.

definition.citation: Renunciation and Realisation — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 21 (1988), 1988-07-11
definition.quote: Vairagya means giving up association with objects, while recognising their inherent worth.

discourses.citation: Forget the Non-Self and Contemplate on the Self (Alternative Translation) — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 29 (1996), 1996-07-04
discourses.quote: Real renunciation lies in giving up evil qualities. This is real renunciation (thyaga) and yoga. … Instead, give up evil qualities, evil practices, ego, and unsacred feelings that are present in you. This is true renunciation.

discourses.citation: You And I — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 3 (1963), 1963-09-08
discourses.quote: The first sign of spiritual life is detachment (vairagyam). If you have no detachment, you are illiterate as far as spiritual scholarship is concerned. Detachment is the ABC of spiritual effort.

discourses.citation: Eternal Truths Should Form The Subject Of Books — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 40 (2007), 2007-08-24
discourses.quote: What is meant by vairagya? It means reducing your desires. Do not go on increasing your desires day by day. … You can be always happy when you reduce your desires.

discourses.citation: Atma is the Fundamental Basis of Everything (Alternative Translation) — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 29 (1996), 1996-09-10
discourses.quote: I do not want you all to become sanyasins and to give up everything. All that I want you to do is to carry on your duties, place your faith in God and realise that there is one fundamental Reality underlying all things. When you get this realisation, detachment will develop in you of its own accord.

make_it_real: You don't have to leave your home to be detached — just leave your desires behind.
title: Detachment (Vairagya)

vahinis.quote: Renunciation or detachment (vairagya), of course, does not mean the giving up of hearth and home, or of high estate and even kingdoms. It is the understanding of the divinity immanent in everything, the fading away of all the distinct names and forms, the bliss of experiencing in everything and every place the Divine, which is its reality.
